column1: Inconsistent validation when deleting all questions individually vs bulk delete in assessment creation
column39:
While creating an assessment, there is inconsistent behavior when removing all questions:

* When deleting questions *one by one*, the system blocks deletion of the last question and shows the validation message:
_“At least one question is required.”_
* However, when selecting *all questions and deleting them via bulk delete*, all questions are removed successfully, and the assessment is saved with *zero questions* without showing any validation error.

This creates confusion, as both actions result in the same state (no questions), but the validation is applied only in the individual delete flow.

*Current Behavior:*

* Individual delete: Validation prevents removing the last question.
* Bulk delete: All questions can be removed, cart becomes empty, and assessment remains in draft state.

Final solution for CDP and same we should implement on the PDF:

# There would be 2 columns in the CDP, Expected Vs Candidate response
# Depending on the usecase, if the system has the correct answer of a question, we should show the Expected Vs Candidate response, if not then there might be manual or AI involvement needed, If “Auto score using AI“ enabled then we should show the what AI has answered for that question in the Expected response, if not we should only show Candidate response with “To be scored“ badge, by this way it would be easier for employer to assess candidate

----

Currently, the *Fill in the Blanks (FIB)* questions do not have a proper visual layout defined for the PDF report. The existing rendering looks inconsistent and difficult to read compared to the web version.

We need a *UX design* for how FIB questions should appear in the PDF reports to ensure readability, consistency, and alignment with other question types.

column1: Candidate side - Merge "Incomplete submission" and "Incomplete mandatory question" popup message
column39:
{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Problem statement: 

* Before the new DISC (MOST and LEAST) flow, when a candidate tries to submit a company test without attempting all questions while time is still remaining, the system displays a “Submit confirmation” popup.
** For “Submit confirmation”, the body text is: “You still have time remaining. Once you submit, you won’t be able to return to this section. Do you want to submit?”, this popup appears when the candidate has attempted all questions but submits the test before the time expires
** For “Incomplete submission”, the body text is: “You have not attempted all the questions in this test. To ensure accurate evaluation, please review and complete all unanswered questions before submitting. Unanswered questions: 28”, this popup is triggered when a candidate attempts to submit a company test with one or more unanswered questions
** For “Incomplete mandatory questions“, the body text is: “Some questions in this test are mandatory and must be answered before submission. Ensure all mandatory questions are addressed before continuing. To ensure accurate evaluation, please review and complete all unanswered questions before submitting.“
* In this scenario, i suggested updating the popup to a generic message that can be reused across all test libraries. The proposed body text was: “You still have time remaining. Some questions are either unanswered or partially attempted. Once you submit, you won’t be able to return to this assessment. Do you want to submit now?”
* However, currently candidates are seeing both popups one after the other (“Submit confirmation” and “Incomplete submission”), depending on the remaining time, which should not happen.
* Expected behavior by scenario:
** Candidate has attempted all questions before time expires: Show “Submit confirmation” popup
** Candidate skips one or more questions and tries to submit before time expires: Show “Incomplete submission” popup
** Candidate has skipped any mandatory question: Show “Incomplete mandatory questions“ popup
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Proposed solution (applies to all company test): 

* Instead of showing three different popups for different use cases, let’s merge “Incomplete submission” and “Incomplete mandatory questions.” If a candidate skips even a single question, whether mandatory or non-mandatory, the test is considered incomplete from the systems perspective. The popup title “Incomplete submission” will remain unchanged. However, the body text should be updated as follows:
* Current body text:
Some questions in this test are mandatory and must be answered before submission. Ensure all mandatory questions are addressed before continuing. To ensure accurate evaluation, please review and complete all unanswered questions before submitting.
* Proposed body text:
You have not completed all the required questions in this test. Some questions are still pending and may be mandatory. Please review the unanswered questions and complete all required items before submitting for evaluation.
Unanswered questions: 28 and 29
{panel}

column1: Don't show ADP for draft assessments
column39:
Two issues:

* If no test/questions added, redirect to assessment list page vs ADP
* When you move fast when creating assessment, An error occurred keeps coming.

h2. *Create assessment flow*

# If the assessment has no tests or questions, after saving, the employer should be redirected to the assessment listing page (ALP) instead of the ADP.

h2. *Edit assessment flow*

# Assessment == Blank (i.e. No tests or questions added)
## The employer should be redirected to the assessment listing page (*ALP*) after saving, *unless the assessment has at least one test or question.*
# Assessment != Blank (i.e. Atleast one test/question added)
## The employer should be redirected to the assessment detail page (*ADP*) after saving.

column1: Add validation for invalid file upload in File Upload & Practical questions when AI scoring is enabled
column39:
h1. Solution for file upload and practical question:

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
Suggestion from UX perspective: 

# There should be standardization in both cases (with or without AI scoring). We should display all the supported file types in both scenarios on the candidate side. It should not depend on whether AI scoring is enabled in both cases, the system should show the acceptable file types upfront on both the candidate and employer sides.
# There might be chances where a candidate uploads a file type that the employer cannot open on their end. To avoid this, it's better that the employer defines the acceptable file types while creating the question. For example, if i want to assess a candidate’s design skills, i may use a file upload or a practical question for the assessment, but if i only use the “Figma” tool, then having the option to allow only .fig files on the employer side would prevent unnecessary back-and-forth.
{panel}

# File upload/Practical: There is no provision for employer to select the file types, so candidate can select any file type if “Auto score using AI“ is not selected, and if enable candidate will have to upload only supported file types that AI supports
# Show message upfront which are the supported file types on the candidate side
## Even after showing message upfront, if candidate uploads non-supported file, so an inline error message after selecting wrong file type if possible, or show an inline-error message and toast message once candidate hits submit button or try moving to next question 
## We can similarly disable “Submit“ button incase of custom question and show in-line error message
!image-20251127-074040.png|width=733,alt="image-20251127-074040.png"!
{color:#36b37e}In-line error message: “Unsupported file type. Please upload a valid format.“{color}

----

*Workspace: White label*

## Question level scoring without auto score using AI
## Question level scoring with auto score using AI

## Criteria level scoring with auto score using AI
# Candidated status: Completed the assessment without any issue
# CDP view before “To be scored“
!image-20251126-142218.png|width=757,alt="image-20251126-142218.png"!

# CDP view after manual scoring is done
!image-20251126-142422.png|width=757,alt="image-20251126-142422.png"!

----

Currently, when a candidate uploads an invalid file type in *File Upload* and *Practical* question types, no validation message is shown. If *AI scoring is enabled*, the system is unable to score the invalid file and the response appears with a *“To be scored”* badge in the CDP.

To improve this flow, a validation message should be displayed *only when AI scoring is enabled*, preventing unsupported file types from being uploaded.
If *AI scoring is disabled*, candidates should be allowed to upload any file type and *no validation message should be shown*.

----

h3. Requirements / Acceptance Criteria

# *When AI scoring is enabled:*
#* The system should validate the file type during upload.
#* If the uploaded file type is not supported:
#** A clear validation message should be shown (e.g., _“This file type is not supported for AI scoring. Please upload a valid file format.”_).
#** The file upload should be blocked.
#** The candidate should not be able to proceed with an invalid file.
#* Only supported file types should be allowed.
# *When AI scoring is disabled:*
#* No file type validation should be applied.
#* Candidates can upload *any file type*.
#* No validation message should be shown.

----

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Create a test with a *File Upload* or *Practical* question.
# Enable *AI scoring*.
# Upload an unsupported file type (e.g. {{.mov}}, {{.mp4}}).
# Observe that no validation is currently shown and the answer appears as *“To be scored”* in CDP.

----

h3. Current Behavior

* Invalid file types can be uploaded without any validation.
* When AI scoring is enabled, corresponding answers in CDP show *“To be scored”* because AI cannot process the file.

----

h3. Expected Behavior

* Validation is triggered only when AI scoring is enabled.
* Unsupported file types are blocked.
* Supported file types are accepted and processed correctly.
* No validation is shown when AI scoring is disabled.

----

# Should “Invitation Type” appear in the Logs? Yes
## From an employer’s perspective, knowing how a candidate entered the assessment is valuable, especially when:
### They need to trace back issues (e.g., “Why did this candidate skip name/email? → They came via Public link.”)
### They want to audit funnel quality (Public vs Bulk vs API).
### They are debugging data mismatch, duplicate profiles, or CSV upload issues.
### They want to confirm if the candidate was invited manually or automatically.

* All static content on the *candidate-facing test portal*, including UI elements, predefined text, instructions, and labels, must also be available in *Arabic*.

----

h3. *Requirements:*

* Translate all static content into Arabic.
* Ensure correct formatting and text alignment based on *Arabic language conventions*.
* Address punctuation issues — for example, full stops should appear on the *right side* of the sentence, not the left (as in English).
* Maintain visual consistency and readability in right-to-left (RTL) format.

----

h3. *Current Issue:*

The portal currently displays English punctuation and alignment even when Arabic is used, which may confuse users and disrupt readability.

----

h3. *Expected Outcome:*

* All static content is properly translated and formatted in Arabic.
* Text is right-aligned, and punctuation appears in the correct positions according to Arabic writing rules.
* Improved user experience for Arabic-speaking candidates.

column1: Add message for unattempted test cases in all psychometric reports
column39:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Scope:

* CDP
* PDF Reports
{panel}

h1. Problem statement: 

For any psychometric test where the candidate has not attempted any questions, display a message: "The candidate has either not attempted the test or answered less than 10% of the questions. As a result, the report is inconclusive. We recommend the candidate retake the test to enable a valid assessment." This will help in providing clear guidance for cases where no questions are answered.[^Prashant Ahire - SMART - Personality.pdf] 

h1. R1)

* The graph data would remain as it is, we just need to add a message on the top incase of test is either fully completed or incomplete.

!image-20250630-141212.png|width=298,height=421,alt="image-20250630-141212.png"!

column1: Feature - Compare candidates
column39:
h1. Scope

# Candidate Comparison Feature Requirements
## Employers can only compare candidates who have completed the assessment.
## If an employer attempts to compare candidates with incomplete assessments or different statuses, the system will display a prompt message: *"Only candidates who have completed the assessment can be compared."*
## In the initial phase, employers can compare up to *three candidates* in a full-screen pop-up mode.
# Candidate Card Details:
## *Candidate Name & Email* (Name can be null)
## *Cancel Option* to remove a candidate from the comparison
## *AI Verdict:* Suggested hiring decision based on assessment performance
## *Technical Score & Time Taken* displayed with a grading badge
# AI-Driven Insights:
## AI identifies key *comparison parameters* based on the assessment
## *Text & Graphical Representation* (Line Graph) for performance metrics
## Performance indicated using *Red (Poor), Yellow (Average), Green (Good)* color coding
## AI highlights *Strengths & Improvement Areas* in bullet format
# Call-to-Action (CTA) for Each Candidate:
## *Shortlist*
## *Reject*
## *View More Details* (Redirects to the candidate’s detail page)
# AI will *highlight the best-performing candidate card*, with *"Shortlist"* as the primary CTA.

column1: Suggestion to Display "Not Applicable" Badge for Non-Scorable Questions
column39:
h1. Possible solution for below issue:

Instead of displaying the “Not Applicable” badge or leaving it blank (as we currently do for custom questions), we should introduce a new badge for non-scorable questions labeled as “Non-Scorable.”

Design: [https://www.figma.com/design/E7Nc2pfC2PnE5wYgX9sZuc/TF---Product?node-id=68704-1487077&recovery=true&t=0GjgawAXjPXWEtpz-11|https://www.figma.com/design/E7Nc2pfC2PnE5wYgX9sZuc/TF---Product?node-id=68704-1487077&recovery=true&t=0GjgawAXjPXWEtpz-11|smart-link] 

*Case 1:* The entire assessment consists of non-scorable questions.

!image-20250325-112752.png|width=750,height=1290,alt="image-20250325-112752.png"!

{color:#0747a6}_Note: This solution is exclusive of psychometric test_{color}

*Case 2:* A company test includes a mix of scorable and non-scorable questions.

!image-20250325-114003.png|width=750,height=1321,alt="image-20250325-114003.png"!

----

I created an assessment that includes both *custom questions* and a *company test*, with non-scorable questions in both. When a candidate attempts the test, I noticed the following behavior on *CDP*:

* For *custom questions*, no scores are displayed (which is correct).
* For *company test* questions, it currently shows *"null%"*, which can be confusing.

I suggest displaying a *"Not Applicable"* badge instead of "null%".

column1: Restrict submitting the typing test before typing test timer ends
column39:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Scope: Typing test question attempt
{panel}



What if a person we smartly types few words correctly, accurately and submits it in some time. They are currently scored with good score.

* Design: [https://www.figma.com/design/Dc2nNubde8Sdsk9IaJYstS/TF---Candidate?node-id=4066-83652&t=xVadJtMwf3IozKtw-11|https://www.figma.com/design/Dc2nNubde8Sdsk9IaJYstS/TF---Candidate?node-id=4066-83652&t=xVadJtMwf3IozKtw-11|smart-link] 

h2. *Submission button before timer is 0*

* *Disabled state:* The “Submit/Next” button should be disabled until the typing test timer reaches zero.
* *Tooltip:* If the user hovers over the disabled button, a tooltip should explain:
** _"_You can submit once the timer ends._"_
** !image-20250404-151552.png|width=327,height=91,alt="image-20250404-151552.png"!
** _"_Question will auto-submit once the timer ends._"_


h2. *Auto-submit after timer is 0*

* *Enabled state:* 
** Once the timer reaches zero, the button becomes active for submission. Anyways we auto-submit and show the type score after that.
* *Auto-submit on timer expiry* 
** If strict timing is required, the system can *automatically submit* the response when the timer hits zero.

----

One should not be able to submit the typing test before Timer ends.

h1. Technical reference:

h2. What % of this exact text is likely AI-generated?

h3. {Text} JSON Response:

{noformat}{
  “AI_generated_likelihood_percent”: 70,
  “reason”: [
    “The text is well-structured and coherent, with formal language and minimal stylistic flair.“,
    “It uses polished phrasing like ‘driven by the founding team’s firsthand experiences’ and ‘highlighted the need’ — common in AI-generated mission statements or origin stories.“,
    “The tone is consistent, informative, and lacks personal or anecdotal voice typically present in genuine founder-written narratives.“,
    “It reads like a refined summary, likely generated or heavily edited using AI tools to craft a professional company backstory.”
  ]
}{noformat}

GPTZero API provide following outputconfidence_category - string - Allowed values: high, medium, low
confidence_score - number - A normalized confidence scoreresult_message - string - Possible values as below

{noformat}"Our detector is highly confident that the text is written by AI"

"Our detector is highly confident that the text may include parts written by AI"

"Our detector is highly confident that the text is written entirely by a human"

"Our detector is moderately confident that the text is written by AI"

"Our detector is moderately confident that the text may include parts written by AI"

"Our detector is moderately confident that the text is written entirely by a human"

"Our detector is highly uncertain about this document. The writing style and content are not particularly AI-like"{noformat}

document_classification

{noformat}The simple classification of the document into:

"HUMAN_ONLY" - high likelihood this text is predominantly written by a human

"MIXED" - either a certain section of this document has a strong signature of being AI generated, or the overall document has a weak signature of being AI-generated

"AI_ONLY" - The document was entirely written by AI{noformat}

h1. Original request:

*Workspace*: Cybercc 

*Lead Status*: Moved to alternate solution

*Plan Considered*: Business Plan + Integration

*Reason for Drop-off*:
Client was satisfied with Chat AI and AI Scoring features but had a critical concern regarding *detection of ChatGPT-generated responses*.

During our call, they clearly mentioned:

* They are fine with candidates Googling or searching answers.
* But they *strictly want to detect if the response was generated using ChatGPT or similar AI tools*.
* The full-screen proctoring feature to detect window-switching was not enough for their use case.

They are satisfied with candidates using search engines but strictly want to detect if responses are generated using AI tools like ChatGPT. column1: Suggestion to Display "Not Applicable" Badge for Non-Scorable Questions
column39:
h1. Possible solution for below issue:

Instead of displaying the “Not Applicable” badge or leaving it blank (as we currently do for custom questions), we should introduce a new badge for non-scorable questions labeled as “Non-Scorable.”

Design: [https://www.figma.com/design/E7Nc2pfC2PnE5wYgX9sZuc/TF---Product?node-id=68704-1487077&recovery=true&t=0GjgawAXjPXWEtpz-11|https://www.figma.com/design/E7Nc2pfC2PnE5wYgX9sZuc/TF---Product?node-id=68704-1487077&recovery=true&t=0GjgawAXjPXWEtpz-11|smart-link] 

*Case 1:* The entire assessment consists of non-scorable questions.

!image-20250325-112752.png|width=750,height=1290,alt="image-20250325-112752.png"!

{color:#0747a6}_Note: This solution is exclusive of psychometric test_{color}

*Case 2:* A company test includes a mix of scorable and non-scorable questions.

!image-20250325-114003.png|width=750,height=1321,alt="image-20250325-114003.png"!

----

I created an assessment that includes both *custom questions* and a *company test*, with non-scorable questions in both. When a candidate attempts the test, I noticed the following behavior on *CDP*:

* For *custom questions*, no scores are displayed (which is correct).
* For *company test* questions, it currently shows *"null%"*, which can be confusing.

I suggest displaying a *"Not Applicable"* badge instead of "null%".

## Trigger an email type prompt with the pre-filled message.

{noformat}Subject: Translation request - {TEST_NAME} to {LANGUAGE_NAME}
Body:

Hi Testlify Assessment Team,

I’d like to translate {TEST_NAME} in {LANGUAGE_NAME}. 

Here are my workspace details:
Workspace Name: XXX
Workspace URL: XXX
Plan: (Paid OR Free trial)
User Name: XXX

### Subject: {TEST_NAME} is now available in {LANGUAGE_NAME}

Hi {FIRST_NAME},

The {TEST_NAME} test is now available in {LANGUAGE_NAME}.

Best,
Team Testlify OR {RESELLER_NAME}

!image-20250401-135627.png|width=654,height=337,alt="image-20250401-135627.png"!

A new *Metabase report* should track:

* Who has translated which *test library* into which *language*
* *Timestamp* of the translation
* *Workspace URL* where the translation occurred

*Columns:*

* Workspace URL
* Test name
* Translation language
* Translated test name
* User initiated
* User email
* Timestamp

h1. +Thoughts from UI side+

Having two active timers during a typing test could indeed create confusion and increase the chances of human errors. Here’s a UX-focused analysis of the situation:

h3. Potential Issues with Two Timers:

# *Cognitive Overload*: Displaying two timers simultaneously can overwhelm the candidate. They may struggle to focus on the task at hand if they’re constantly distracted by the ticking of both timers.
# *Stress and Anxiety*: Timers inherently add pressure. Having two can heighten anxiety, leading to poor performance, especially in something like a typing test where concentration is key.
# *Attention Split*: Candidates might inadvertently focus on the wrong timer (e.g., the overall assessment timer instead of the typing test timer), leading to timing errors or a rushed test.

h3. Possible Solutions:

# *Single Timer Approach*: Show only the typing test timer during that specific task. The overall assessment timer could be paused, hidden, or only shown in a minimized format to avoid distraction.
# *Integrated Timer*: Another approach could be integrating the two timers, where the assessment timer automatically adjusts or pauses during the typing test. This approach ensures that the candidate is only aware of the time relevant to the current task.
# *Contextual Information*: If keeping both timers is necessary, provide clear contextual information or visual cues that distinguish their purposes. For example, the assessment timer could be displayed more subtly, while the typing test timer is more prominent.

h3. Recommendation:

I recommend *pausing the overall assessment timer during the typing test* and displaying only the typing test timer. This way, candidates can focus entirely on the typing task without the distraction or stress of managing multiple timers. If pausing the assessment timer isn’t feasible, making the assessment timer less prominent and ensuring clear instructions about how the timing works would be crucial to minimize confusion.

This approach balances user focus and reduces cognitive load, leading to a smoother and less error-prone experience.

----

When deciding when to display results during a time-based assessment, especially one that includes a typing test, it's crucial to consider the impact on user experience, focus, and performance. Here’s an analysis:

h3. Displaying Results *During* the Test:

* *Distractions*: Showing results during the test can be distracting. For instance, if a candidate sees their typing speed or accuracy immediately after finishing a typing test, it might affect their focus on the remaining parts of the assessment.
* *Pressure and Anxiety*: Immediate feedback can increase pressure. If a candidate sees that they performed poorly on one section, it might negatively impact their confidence and performance in subsequent sections.
* *Breaking Flow*: Displaying results during the test can interrupt the candidate's flow and rhythm, particularly if they must mentally switch between assessment modes and result interpretation.

h3. Displaying Results *After* the Test:

* *Maintains Focus*: Candidates can concentrate fully on each section of the test without worrying about immediate feedback. This approach supports a smoother and more consistent testing experience.
* *Holistic Evaluation*: By displaying results at the end, candidates receive a comprehensive view of their performance across the entire assessment, allowing them to understand their strengths and weaknesses in context.
* *Reduced Stress*: Waiting until the end to display results can reduce the stress and anxiety associated with instant feedback. Candidates can focus on doing their best without being influenced by earlier performance.

h3. Recommendation:

I recommend displaying the *results after the completion of the entire test*. This approach ensures that candidates can maintain focus throughout the assessment without distractions or added pressure. Once the test is completed, a detailed breakdown of the results, including individual section scores and any relevant feedback, can be presented.

column1: Templates & Presets for Assessment Settings & Proctoring
column39:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Employers should be able to select a predefined assessment configuration using three tabs:

* *Standard (Default)* – Balanced security with flexible navigation.
* *Strict* – High security with strict proctoring and restricted navigation.
* *Custom* – Allows employers to manually adjust all settings.

Selecting a tab should dynamically apply the corresponding settings for *Proctoring* sections.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
If the employer customizes the default options of the "Standard" or "Strict" preset, it should automatically switch to the "Custom" preset.
{panel}

# On selecting each tab, the system should auto-select set of setting options:
## For Standard, following are option should auto-selected and a tooltip message system should show
### Tooltip message: Balanced security with flexible navigation.
## For Strict, following are option should auto-selected
### Tooltip message: High security with strict proctoring and restricted navigation.
## We should keep the “Custom“ tab open, in which all the options are de-selected by-default
### Tooltip message: Manually adjust all settings to fit your needs.
# For Proctoring 
## Standard will enable following options:
### Full-screen mode
### Honesty agreement
### AI assistance detection
## All the proctoring options should be enabled in the strict mode (Except verify private, and dual camera proctoring)

column1: Subscription Cancellation Reason to be made Mandatory when client cancels subscription
column39:
h1. INTERNAL REQUEST

Request by [~accountid:712020:4263f50f-1a47-4205-90d8-5d9ebc997ad5] 

When a client cancels their subscription, there are only a few of them to choose to mention whey they are discontinuing, for most others, the team is regularly following up to get their feedback.

To understand why the client is cancelling the subscription, mentioning the reason for cancellation should be made mandatory. 

This would help in 2 ways: 

a) We will get to know the reason for cancellation and make require improvements to the platform  

b) We would not need to do multiple manually follow-ups, where the response rate is anyway very low.

h2. References for animation libraries:

h3. CSS-Based Libraries:

# *Animate.css*: Fully CSS-based. It uses pre-defined CSS classes to add animations.
# *Element Plus Built-In Transitions*: Some components in Element Plus already include CSS-based transitions that can be customized.

h3. JavaScript-Based Libraries:

# *VueUse*: While it doesn't directly create animations, it provides reactive utilities (like scroll and mouse events) that can be combined with JS-based animations.
# *Framer Motion for Vue*: JavaScript-based with declarative APIs for advanced animations and transitions.
# *GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform)*: Fully JavaScript-based, designed for detailed and high-performance animations.
# *VueUse Motion*: JavaScript-based, leveraging {{motion}} to define animations declaratively.

h3. JSON/Asset-Based:

# *Lottie*: Uses JSON files to render animations via JavaScript and the browser.

h3. Hybrid:

# *VueTransition (Vue's built-in transition system)*: Combines CSS for animations and JavaScript for event-driven logic.

## Updated copy “Use the single sign-on authentication policy to require all members to log in with SSO.“

### Sub-text 
### Tooltip
!image-20240821-062653 (0d97c1e6-e2da-4f6d-9643-a9f854018693).png|width=320,height=154,alt="image-20240821-062653.png"!

## Team slug
### Text field and a button to copy the inputted text
#### Initially, the text field will be empty, and the button to copy text will also be in a disabled state.

!image-20240821-062558 (ce9152d2-d377-4125-9e2b-37fa03720eb2).png|width=320,height=112,alt="image-20240821-062558.png"!
## Type
### The type will be SAML by default and this field will be disabled.
## Service provider URLs 
### Tooltip
!image-20240821-062147 (22b589cf-9991-4fa5-8d96-b3534c007298).png|width=320,height=217,alt="image-20240821-062147.png"!
### In this section we have 2 sub-sections, each will have a “Copy text“ button:
#### Entity URL 
#### Consumer service URL
## Identity providers 
### Tooltip
!image-20240821-061839 (29cec190-e2b6-411d-b089-0ed12b8410d1).png|width=320,height=175,alt="Tooltip message"!

h3. Identity providers (CRUD)

# At the initial stage, this section would be empty
# The “Add“ option will allow the employer to add a new identity provider
# The add new identity journey will be handled on a separate page
## The system will ask following details to create a new “Identity provider“
### Name
### Entity ID
### SSO URL
### Public x509 certificate
## The employer will be redirected to the SSO SAML page by clicking on the back button at the top.
## The newly created “Identity provider“ will be shown in a tabular format under the “Identity provider“ section on the “SSO SAML“ page
### The table would have the following attribute and an action button
#### Name
#### Status
#### The action button will have the following options:
##### Edit
##### Delete ({color:#0747a6}_Note: On deletion the employer will get a “Confirm deletion” prompt_{color})
!image-20240821-115640 (07165cb6-a821-486a-9fe9-ec6710e9d7d9).png|width=300,height=163,alt="image-20240821-115640.png"!
##### Enable or Disable ({color:#0747a6}_Note: When an Identity provider is enabled, the disable option will appear on the menu, and vice versa, also when disable the employer will get “Confirm disable“ prompt_{color}) 
!image-20240821-115628 (84e4f149-cbec-468d-a76f-17a21aa08612).png|width=300,height=163,alt="image-20240821-115628.png"!
## Add new Identity Providers' user journey
### From the "Add+" button, this journey will be triggered
### Employers will be redirected to a separate page when they click "Add+", where they will need to enter the following information:
#### Name
#### Entity ID
#### SSO URL
#### Public x509 certificate
#### Status ({color:#0747a6}_Note: By default this would be in disabled state_{color})
### Once all the mandatory fields have been filled in, the "Save" button will become active
### The employer will be redirected to the SAML SSO page after saving the data
### If the employer clicks on the back button while creating the Identity Provider, all data will be discarded
## Edit existing Identity providers user journey ({color:#0747a6}_Note: The “Edit“ journey would be same as “Add+“ new Identity provider_{color})
### Once the identity provider is created the employer would be able to view entity url and consumer service url on the edit page

*Summary:*

A client [scitaris.testlify.com|http://scitaris.testlify.com] has expressed confusion regarding the scoring logic for the "Fill in the Blank" question type in the assessment system. Specifically, when multiple options are added to the blank field (e.g., text options), all of them are considered correct answers and are scored fully if selected. The system should be updated to include a notification in the UI to inform employers that any options added to the blank field will be treated as correct answers.

*Requirement*:

Implement a UI update to notify employers that when they add multiple options to a blank (e.g., Text) in a "Fill in the Blank" question, all the options will be treated as correct answers and will be fully scored if selected.

Ensure this clarification is clearly visible to employers during the creation of the question to avoid confusion.

* When there is a duplication in the answer options.
* When any of the answer or score fields are empty.

# Add a new question.
# In the "Options" field, enter the following values:
#* {{op2}}
#* {{op2}} (duplicate option)
#* {{op3}}
#* {{op4}}
# Attempt to save or submit the question with the provided options.

h3. *Expected Result:*

* The system should display an error message that clearly indicates a duplicate option is present, and the error message should appear next to the specific duplicate options ({{op2}} in this case).

* The error message ("Option already exists. Please enter a unique option") is shown only after the last option field ({{op4}}), instead of directly next to the duplicate option ({{op2}}).

column1: AI search and filtering on ADP
column39:
h1. Current UX issues related to search

# *Inconsistency*: Users may not clearly understand where to search for what.
# *Cognitive Load*: Switching between searches for different content types can confuse users.

h3. 1. *Universal Search Enhancements*

* The universal search (at the top of the page) becomes an *"All-in-One Search"* with:
** A *default view* that prioritizes *candidates* (to match current behavior).
** An *auto-categorization* feature: Search results are grouped by content types (e.g., Candidates, Assessments, Tests, Questions, Templates).
** Filters within search results to allow users to refine by *content type*.
** A fallback message: “No results found for Candidates. Try searching across other content types.”

UI Adjustments for Universal Search:

* Add a *dropdown* or inline filter toggle within the universal search bar:
** *Default*: "Search candidates"
** *Options*: "Search all content," "Search Assessments," "Search Library."
** Make this dynamic—if users type "test," show results from *Tests* first.

h3. *2. Page-Specific Search Optimizations*

* Retain page-level searches since they provide focused control and filters.
* *Visual Differentiation*: Highlight the scoped nature of page-specific searches (e.g., "Search Tests" in Tests Library, "Search Candidates" on Candidates Page).

----

h3. Sample prompt

# Status
## Show me candidates who are currently enrolled or in progress with their assessment.
## Find candidates with completed assessments.
## Who has been disqualified or rejected?
## List candidates with invitation statuses marked as 'expired'.
# Stage
## Find candidates who were invited for an interview.
## Show me who has been shortlisted or has an offer sent.
## Locate candidates not yet evaluated or who withdrew their application.
## List all candidates with completed assessments but haven’t been shortlisted yet.
# Grading
## Show me candidates graded as 'expert' or 'experienced'.
## Filter out candidates with a grade of 'not suitable' or 'beginner'.
## Find all intermediate candidates who have completed their assessments.
# Invitation Type
## List candidates invited individually for the assessment.
## Find all candidates who responded to bulk invitations.
## Who applied through the public invitation link?
# Date Completed
## Show me all candidates who completed their assessments today or yesterday.
## Find candidates who finished their assessments this month.
## Who completed assessments last year but hasn’t been evaluated yet?
# Label
## Find candidates with the label 'Priority'.
## Show all candidates marked as 'Follow-Up Needed'.
## List candidates with no labels assigned.
# Invited By
## List all candidates invited by [Recruiter Name].
## Who were invited by [Recruiter Name] in the last month?
## Find candidates not invited by any recruiter.
# Additional combined prompts:
## Show candidates graded as 'proficient' who were shortlisted for an interview last week.
## Find all candidates invited in bulk who are currently in progress or have completed their assessments.
## List 'expert' candidates with offers sent this month.

h3. Error-states samples:

# If a user applies incompatible filters (e.g., _Status: Completed_ + _Stage: Not Evaluated_), AI detects the conflict and suggests corrections:
## Status: Completed cannot include Stage: Not Evaluated. Adjust one of the filters.
